requirements.title: CFI_address has the ISO_Fortran_binding.h address-query interface
requirements.definition: CFI_address has the interface void *CFI_address(const CFI_cdesc_t *dv, const CFI_index_t subscripts[]) and returns the C address of an object described by a C descriptor.

pending.CFI_address-interface: C companion includes ISO_Fortran_binding.h, declares a CFI_cdesc_t pointer and a CFI_index_t subscript array, and compiles an ordinary CFI_address call returning void * without suppressing any macro.

requirements.oracle: Source registration only. Future mixed Fortran/C fixtures compile a C companion with the processor ISO_Fortran_binding.h, link it with a Fortran driver through the existing C interoperability harness, and assert only portable descriptor members, pointer equality or address differences computed from descriptor storage strides, CFI_SUCCESS equal to zero, named CFI error macros by identity rather than numeric value, and exact integer/logical status results. Numeric values of error macros other than CFI_SUCCESS, C object padding, alignment choices beyond successful creation, allocation addresses, and selection among several detected errors remain processor latitude.

requirements.title: CFI_address actual arguments must describe an associated object and valid subscripts
requirements.definition: The descriptor argument shall describe an object that is neither an unallocated allocatable variable nor a disassociated pointer; array subscripts shall provide at least rank elements within descriptor bounds, with the stated assumed-size exception.

pending.CFI_address-dv-describes-associated-obje: Positive C companion first establishes a descriptor with nonnull base storage and nonzero extent, then calls CFI_address; a disassociated-pointer call is nonconforming and carries no required diagnostic facet.
pending.CFI_address-subscript-array-rank-and-bou: Use rank-two extents 3 by 4 and subscripts {2,1}, both within descriptor lower and upper bounds; companion mutation changes one subscript beyond the extent as a source-control negative only.
pending.CFI_address-assumed-size-last-subscript-: No portable source-only C companion creates the required assumed-size descriptor state; future mixed fixture obtains such a descriptor from Fortran and asserts only addresses for subscripts not below the last lower bound and not beyond actual size.

requirements.title: CFI_address returns the address of the selected array element or scalar object
requirements.definition: For a rank-n array, the result is the C address of the element selected by the first n subscripts; for a scalar, the result is its C address.

pending.CFI_address-array-element-address: C companion establishes a rank-two source descriptor over int storage with extents 3 and 4, then uses CFI_setpointer with lower_bounds {2,-1} to produce a rank-two pointer descriptor with explicit nonzero lower bounds. With subscripts {4,1}, it asserts CFI_address returns base_addr + (4-2)*dim[0].sm + (1-(-1))*dim[1].sm using char-pointer arithmetic, and the referenced element holds the prefilled sentinel value at element offset 8.
pending.CFI_address-scalar-address: C companion establishes a rank-zero descriptor for an int initialized to 314159, calls CFI_address with a null subscript pointer, and asserts the returned pointer equals the address of that int and dereferences to 314159.

review_rationale: Source registration for 18.5.5 and 18.5.5.1-18.5.5.9, the functions declared in ISO_Fortran_binding.h: CFI_address, CFI_allocate, CFI_deallocate, CFI_establish, CFI_is_contiguous, CFI_section, CFI_select_part and CFI_setpointer (batch244). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across three rounds; success paths and isolated named-error conditions are planned as C companion programs with exact results. Source accounting only.
